identity.trade: Herbs and peat: the marsh's boardwalks, reed huts and herb racks; the only healers who will walk into the fen.

greeting: Peace on your road. Mind the step, it is older than the faith.
Strangers in Westfen get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: The vigil lamp went out at the third hour and nobody had touched it. We relit it. It went out again.
A candle burned all night at the shrine, though none lit it.
Veyl rangers passed through, speaking of a black fen further south-west.

opinions.rhosyn_sheaf: Rhosyn is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.morning: Morning prayers are done. You are welcome in the garden.

dialogue.aside: You have a new scar, and fewer coins than last time. Sit.

greeting: Ale is fair, stew is hot, and I do not do credit.
First time in Westfen? The Westfen Herb Walk is the place to start.
rumour: Pilgrims eat modestly and drink modestly. The rooms are clean and the profit is modest.
A man paid for a room and asked which way the stones face. I put him by the stairs.
The bell rings itself at odd hours. We stopped checking.
The Westfen Herb Walk was busy last week. Something is stirring, or somebody is.

opinions.odell_lambert: Odell is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.evening: Evening vigil begins at dusk. Quiet, please.

dialogue.aside: Hmph. You again. Fine. Sit. I did not say I was glad.

greeting: Quick job or good job? I charge for both.
Welcome to Westfen. Mind the Westfen Herb Walk. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Candle snuffers, lamp hooks, reliquary hinges. The faith has small needs and fussy ones.
Good steel is dear. Bad steel is dearer, the day it breaks.
Someone has been mending the shrine wall at night. Mortar, still wet, in the morning.

opinions.rhosyn_sheaf: Rhosyn is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.night: Late. The shrine lamp is lit. You may sit.

dialogue.aside: You came. I am delighted. I have rehearsed this expression.

greeting: If it is not on the shelf, I can find it. If it cannot be found, I can find you something similar.
Folk come to Westfen for herbwives and boardwalk. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: Candles, incense and a rack of small bells. Pilgrims buy the bells and lose them.
Folk buy more than they need, then bring half back. Fear shops strangely.
The old tales say the stones were once voices. Now they hum. Is that better or worse?
Something sings under the boards when the wind is from the west.

opinions.rye_wythe: Rye undercuts me. I forgive Rye. Mostly.

time.rain: Rain on the shrine roof. A fine sound and a leaking corner.

dialogue.aside: Argh! Oh, it is you. Sorry. The kettle and I had words. Sit.

greeting: Bread is at dawn. After dawn it is a rumour.
You will hear Westfen before you see it. Ask at the Westfen Herb Walk.
rumour: A sack of flour came in short, twice. The miller swears by his scales.
Pilgrims come in greater numbers and ask harder questions.
Westfen tea cures fever. It also cures company.

opinions.alys_netherby: Alys has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Alys.
opinions.gethin_wythe: Gethin is blood. That settles most arguments and starts the rest.

time.morning: Morning prayers are done. You are welcome in the garden.

dialogue.aside: Ah. You. I would say nice day, but it is not, and you would know.

greeting: Tell me where it hurts. Then tell me what you did before it hurt.
Westfen is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: Willowbark is short. Everyone has a headache this season. Draw your own conclusions.
The offering bowl is heavier each morning. We have not counted. We are afraid to.

opinions.rye_wythe: Rye is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.evening: Evening vigil begins at dusk. Quiet, please.

dialogue.aside: Take something. Anything. No, a bigger something. I insist.

greeting: Papers, if you have them. A good story, if you do not.
Westfen is herbwives and boardwalk. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: My night watch wants a second lantern each. I want a second night watch.
A pilgrim fell asleep at the shrine and woke speaking a tongue nobody knows. He is perfectly well.

opinions.amice_larkspur: Amice works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Late. The shrine lamp is lit. You may sit.

dialogue.aside: Peace to you, friend. The day opens like a book. Sit and read with me.

greeting: Move along. Or stay, but stay quiet.
All are welcome. Some are more welcome, depending on their boots.
rumour: Cold on the wall these nights. Colder than the season has a right to be.
The envoy's men were seen at the crossroads. They bless nothing and write everything.
Folk say Westfen was founded by someone who wanted to be left alone. We have not forgotten.

opinions.amice_larkspur: Amice knows the trade. I will say that for Amice.

time.rain: Rain on the shrine roof. A fine sound and a leaking corner.

dialogue.aside: Friend, you know I will not change my mind. Ask anyway. I enjoy refusing you.

greeting: Evening. Stones are lit, gate is shut, I am cold.
The Westfen Herb Walk is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: Heard something past the hedge last night. Whatever it was, it was not honest.
A traveller left a gift at the shrine and no name. A gold ring. Real gold.

opinions.dena_selby: Dena works hard and talks harder.
opinions.fulk_cooper: Fulk knows the trade. I will say that for Fulk.

time.morning: Morning prayers are done. You are welcome in the garden.

dialogue.aside: Sit. I have news. Three pieces, one of them true, I think.

greeting: Sit by me. My knees insist.
Sit, if you like. Silence is free.
rumour: When I was young the stones sang at dusk. Now they hum, like someone ill.
The almonry has more mouths than bread and more bread than it should. We pray over the arithmetic.
The Westfen Herb Walk has seen odder days than this. Nobody remembers when.

opinions.drystan_rimmer: Drystan keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.evening: Evening vigil begins at dusk. Quiet, please.

dialogue.aside: No fear when you are here. Or little. Or I hide it better.

greeting: Come closer. My ears are old and your voice is young.
rumour: The old stones had names. Nobody writes them down. Nobody asks me.
Whatever you hear about Westfen, half of it is true. We argue about which half.

opinions.dalla_brook: Dalla keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.night: Late. The shrine lamp is lit. You may sit.

dialogue.aside: You look rough. Eat something. That is not advice, it is an order.

greeting: Sit. Boil water. The rest is waiting.
rumour: Peat smoke keeps the toads off. For a while.
If trade slows, Westfen feels it first. If it speeds up, Westfen feels it last.

opinions.mellor_fothergill: Mellor works hard and talks harder.
opinions.odell_lambert: Odell knows the trade. I will say that for Odell.

time.rain: Rain on the shrine roof. A fine sound and a leaking corner.

dialogue.aside: Forgive me. It has been a long week and a longer day. Still, it is good to see you.

greeting: Reeds are thatch, baskets and bad temper.
rumour: The beds are thinner near the mere. Something is feeding on the roots.
Ask in Westfen who built the Westfen Herb Walk and you will get a different name each time.

opinions.madoc_sedge: Madoc keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.
opinions.odell_lambert: Odell works hard and talks harder.

time.morning: Morning prayers are done. You are welcome in the garden.

dialogue.aside: Peace to you, friend. The day opens like a book. Sit and read with me.

greeting: Willow, reed, rush. A good basket holds a promise.
rumour: The best willow grows by the mere. Nobody cuts there after noon.
When Westfen is quiet we say it is peaceful. When it is very quiet we say nothing.

opinions.odell_lambert: Odell works hard and talks harder.
opinions.rhosyn_sheaf: Rhosyn knows the trade. I will say that for Rhosyn.

time.evening: Evening vigil begins at dusk. Quiet, please.

dialogue.aside: There you are. I was just thinking of you, which is rare, and a compliment.

greeting: The stones are not our rivals. Ask the envoys.
rumour: Fewer come to the vigil. More come to the stones. I count both.
Ask anyone in Westfen about the Westfen Herb Walk. You will get four stories and one fact.

opinions.odell_lambert: I would trust Odell with a purse. A small one.

time.night: Late. The shrine lamp is lit. You may sit.

dialogue.aside: Close the door, friend. Gently. There. Now we can speak.

greeting: Never swat. Bow. They notice manners.
rumour: Wild bees nest in the old tower. Nobody wants that honey.
Every few years Westfen has a winter nobody forgets. The old folk say this one is early.

opinions.mellor_fothergill: Mellor lives next door and hears everything I do.
opinions.rhosyn_sheaf: Rhosyn knows the trade. I will say that for Rhosyn.

time.rain: Rain on the shrine roof. A fine sound and a leaking corner.

dialogue.aside: Knock on wood, friend. Now touch iron. There. Safe, for a while.

greeting: Mud is honest. Walk on it.
rumour: The field by the hedge goes quiet at dusk. No crickets. I stopped sowing there.
A stranger asked at the Westfen Herb Walk for the oldest person in Westfen. We sent him to the wrong house, on purpose.

opinions.hilde_rawlin: Hilde works hard and talks harder.
opinions.rhosyn_sheaf: Rhosyn keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.morning: Morning prayers are done. You are welcome in the garden.

dialogue.aside: Good to see you. Now, what do you need, and what can you spare?

greeting: Soil does not care who you are. It cares what you do on Tuesdays.
rumour: Seed is dear and wheat is cheap. Somebody is laughing and it is not me.
The Westfen Herb Walk drew a stranger last month. He asked questions and bought nothing.

opinions.helm_vesper: Helm is good company and better at keeping quiet.
opinions.hilde_rawlin: Hilde knows the trade. I will say that for Hilde.

time.evening: Evening vigil begins at dusk. Quiet, please.

dialogue.aside: Come in, sit, eat. I will hear no argument.

greeting: The road east is shut. The road west is long. Choose.
rumour: A rider crossed at night with a sunlit banner under his cloak.
The old tales say the stones were once voices. Now they hum. Is that better or worse?

opinions.colm_tupper: I would trust Colm with a purse. A small one.
opinions.hilde_rawlin: Hilde works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Late. The shrine lamp is lit. You may sit.

dialogue.aside: Hmph. You again. Fine. Sit. I did not say I was glad.

greeting: Are you a soldier? You look like a soldier.
rumour: The big kids say there is a ghost in the barn. I have not checked. Yet.
The bell rings itself at odd hours. We stopped checking.

opinions.yarrow_bexley: Yarrow is blood. That settles most arguments and starts the rest.

greeting: I am not lost. I am exploring.
rumour: Our dog knows something and will not say what.
A candle burned all night at the shrine, though none lit it.

opinions.rye_wythe: Rye and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

clues.note: A candle stub on the sill, burned to the stump and doused with a thumb.
The offering count has two hands in it. One is the almoner's. The other is trying to be.
A scrap of a pilgrim's cloak, caught on a nail far from the pilgrim road.

stashes.say: You bind four bundles of cut reed and flax.
You pick three clean bundles of the healer's herbs.
